title: How an Electric Kettle Works in 60 Seconds ☕⚡ #shorts
description:
Your kettle knows when to stop without any computer. A heating element under the base heats the water, convection spreads the heat, and at boiling point steam is guided to a bimetallic disc. The two metals expand differently, the disc snaps, and the switch clicks off. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#kettle #howitworks #shorts

steps.label: The Secret
steps.text: Your kettle knows when to stop, with no computer. Just *steam* and a clever piece of metal.

steps.label: Heating Element
steps.text: Hidden under the base, a *heating element* turns electric current into heat.

steps.label: Convection
steps.text: Hot water rises and cooler water sinks, so the water *circulates* and heats evenly.

steps.label: Boiling
steps.text: At boiling point, bubbles of *steam* burst up from the bottom.

steps.label: Steam Channel
steps.text: Some steam is guided down a small channel to a *bimetallic* disc by the switch.

steps.label: Click
steps.text: Two metals expand by different amounts, so the disc *snaps* and pushes the switch off.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Heat, boil, steam, *click*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
